statement.p: Find the surface area of the portion S of the cone z^2=x^2+y^2, where z\ge 0,

static.solution:
x=\pm\sqrt{z^2-y^2}.
The projection of the cone onto the yz-plane is obtained by setting x=0 in the equation of the cone, that is, x=0=\sqrt{z^2- y^2} \quad\Rightarrow\quad z=\pm y Since on S, z\ge 0, we get z=|y|. We conclude that the projection of the upper part of the cone x^2+y^2=z^2 onto the yz-plane is
the region between the lines z=y and z=-y on the upper part of the yz-plane.
Therefore, the projection \mathcal{D} of S onto the yz-plane is the region shown in the figure:
With r_0=5
The area of S is the surface integral: \mathrm{Area}(S)=\iint_S \,dS We compute the integral using a surface integral over a graph. Since x=g(y,z)=\pm\sqrt{z^2-y^2} we have, g_z=\pm \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2- y^2}}, \, g_y =\pm \frac{y}{\sqrt{z^2-y^2}} Hence, (notice that z\ge 0 on S): \sqrt{1+ g_y^2+g_z^2} = \sqrt{1+\frac{z^2}{z^2-y^2}+\frac{y^2}{z^2-y^2}} =\sqrt{\frac{2z^2}{z^2-y^2}} = \frac{z\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{z^2-y^2}} We obtain the following integral: \mathrm{Area}(S) =\iint_{\mathcal{D}} \sqrt{1+ g_y^2+ g_z^2} \,dy \,dz= \iint_{\mathcal{D}} \frac{z\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{z^2- y^2}} \,dz \,dy Using symmetry gives: \mathrm{Area}(S) = 4 \int_0^{5/(\sqrt{2})} \int_y^{\sqrt{25-y^2}} \frac{z\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{z^2- y^2}} \,dz \,dy=4\sqrt{2} \int_0^{5/(\sqrt{2})} \left(\int_y^{\sqrt{25- y^2}} \frac{z \,dz}{\sqrt{z^2- y^2}}\right) \,dy \quad \mathbf{(1)} We compute the inner integral using the substitution u=\sqrt{z^2-y^2}, \,du=\frac zu\,dz. We get: \int_y^{\sqrt{25-y^2}} \frac{z\,dz}{\sqrt{z^2-y^2}} = \int_0^{\sqrt{25-2y^2}} \frac{u\,du}{u} =\int_0^{\sqrt{25-2y^2}}\,du=\sqrt{25-2y^2} We substitute in \mathbf{(1)} and compute the resulting integral using the substitution t=\frac1{5}\sqrt{2}y. We get: \mathrm{Area}(S) = 4\sqrt{2} \int_0^{5/(\sqrt{2})} \sqrt{25-2 y^2} \,dy=4\sqrt{2} \int_0^1 \sqrt{25-25 t^2} \frac{5 dt}{\sqrt{2}}=4\cdot {5}^2\int_0^1 \sqrt{1- t^2}\,dt= 4\cdot {5}^2\cdot \frac{\pi}{4}= 25 \pi
